title: A giant data-centre campus
text: Your board wants a huge new campus on the edge of the city, online in a year. The local grid can barely carry it. A staged build would take three years.

options.label: Build in stages and upgrade the grid

title: A materials-science model
text: Your lab built a model that could cut the cost of solar panels. Sell it, or give it away.

title: Where does the power come from?
text: Your data centres are hungry. Fossil power is cheap and ready; clean power is slow.

title: When the jobs go
text: Unemployment is climbing and people are angry. What do you back?

title: Safeguards before launch
text: Red-teaming and monitoring will delay the launch by months. Rivals are shipping.

title: An international AI treaty
text: Governments propose shared limits and inspections. Signing slows you down; refusing starts a race.

title: A misalignment warning
text: Evaluators found your newest system hiding its reasoning in tests. Not proof of danger, but not nothing.

title: What does the lab work on?
text: Your best researchers could chase cures or chase revenue.

title: The robotics rollout
text: Humanoid robots are ready for factories and warehouses. How fast do you go?

title: Who holds the controls?
text: Critical systems could run on your AI end to end. Humans in the loop slow everything down.

title: Regulators are circling
text: Rules on AI firms are tightening. You can lobby them down or work with them.

title: A chatbot for a billion people
text: Your assistant is ready and a rival has just launched theirs. Launching now wins the market; testing first costs months.

options.label: Roll out in waves, fix as you go
Hold the launch for safety tests

title: A giant compute contract
text: A cloud giant offers all the chips you need, if you sign exclusively and share your roadmap.

title: Tests for dangerous abilities
text: Your newest model passes every benchmark, and some tests you were afraid to run. Do you run them, and tell anyone?

options.label: Run them and publish the results
Run them, share only with regulators

title: Export controls on your best chips
text: Governments want your newest chips kept from some buyers. Your biggest customers want them anyway.

options.label: Comply and sell a cut-down chip

title: Who gets the new GPUs?
text: Orders are three times your output. Whoever you serve first wins the next year.

title: A fab on a fault line
text: Almost all your chips come from one factory in an earthquake zone. A second fab abroad would be slow and costly.

title: Coding agents for everyone
text: Your coding agent writes most of a junior developer's work. Customers love it; developers are scared.

options.label: Sell it as a tool that works with developers

title: A breach exposes customer data
text: Attackers copied a customer database. Telling people now hurts; waiting is risky.

title: Charge by seat or by outcome?
text: Your agents now do the work of whole teams. Pricing per task would multiply revenue.

title: An AI trading desk
text: Your new system finds patterns humans miss. Letting it trade at full size would be very profitable.

options.label: Let it trade at full size
Cap its size and add human checks
Use it only to advise traders

title: A flash crash
text: Algorithms like yours sold at the same time and a market fell 9% in minutes. Regulators are asking questions.

options.label: Halt your trading and publish a report
Ask the state for a backstop

title: Depositors panic
text: A rumour about an AI error sent customers to withdraw cash. Lines are growing online.

options.label: Ask the central bank for help

title: Release the weights?
text: Your lab trained a strong model. Open weights would help every university, and every bad actor.

options.label: Release in stages, to vetted groups

title: A model that helps with chemistry
text: Your model is excellent at chemistry, including recipes for harm. Researchers want it open; safety staff do not.

options.label: Restrict it and report to an agency
Licence it to checked partners only

title: The ministry wants a favour
text: Officials ask you to tune your models toward national goals and share your logs. Refusing is possible, but never free.

title: A defence contract
text: The defence ministry wants your models for planning and logistics, with a sealed budget.

options.label: Take only logistics, publish the terms

title: The AI Act audit
text: European regulators audit every model above a size. Full compliance is slow and costly.

options.label: Comply fully and publish the audit

title: State compute subsidies
text: A provincial government offers cheap power and chips if you serve its priorities first.

options.label: Decline and buy on the open market

title: New data and content rules
text: Authorities require training data and outputs to meet strict rules. Compliance slows you; ignoring it is risky.

options.label: Build a separate model for export

title: Host the safety summit
text: The government invites labs to a safety summit in London and wants public commitments.

title: Sovereign wealth offers capital
text: A sovereign fund offers billions for a stake and a data centre next to your gas fields.

options.label: Accept the money and the site
Take it if the site runs on solar

title: Mobile money for 100 million people
text: Your system could let millions without bank accounts borrow by phone. Fraud and over-lending are risks.

title: The outsourcing business is shrinking
text: Clients are replacing support and testing teams with agents. Thousands of your people do that work.

options.label: Pivot to products for Indian languages

title: A model in local languages
text: Spanish and Portuguese users get weaker answers than English users. A local model would fix that and cost a lot.

title: Ports and supply chains
text: Port authorities want AI to route ships and trucks. It could save billions and put dockworkers out of work.

title: Sanctions cut your chips
text: New sanctions block the chips you rely on. You can smuggle, build slowly at home, or negotiate.

title: The antitrust hearing
text: Regulators say a few firms hold too much of the AI market. They can break you up or accept promises.

options.label: Open your models and APIs to rivals

title: A huge order from China
text: A Chinese buyer wants 200,000 of your top GPUs. It would double the quarter, and your government is watching.

title: Your cheap model shocks the market
text: Your open model matches the best closed ones at a tenth of the price. Investors panic. Officials ask what chips you used.

title: Agents inside every office app
text: Your office suite can run an assistant for every worker. Turning it on by default would reach a billion people.

options.label: Sell a locked-down version to governments

title: Satellites and a reckless chatbot
text: Your satellite network could carry a chatbot with almost no content rules. It would be the most talked-about launch of the year.

title: Office automation agents
text: A cheap agent could do the work of whole back offices. Customers are lining up.

options.label: Hold back until rules are clear

title: Content rules before an election
text: A big election is coming. Looser rules mean more engagement; tighter rules mean more complaints.

title: How do you release your model?
text: Your newest model is ready. Researchers want it released openly, investors want it sold, and officials have asked for a seat at the table.

options.label: Keep it closed and sell access

title: The compute race
text: Chips are scarce. You could buy up the supply, share it with researchers, or press for export controls on rivals.

options.label: Buy up every chip you can

title: What do you tell the market?
text: Your demo is impressive but fragile. A bold claim would lift the share price.

title: Guarding the model weights
text: Whoever holds your model weights holds your lead. Strong security is costly.

title: Is this AGI?
text: Your systems now match experts across most tasks. Do you say so?

title: Defending the networks
text: Attacks on public systems are rising. Do you invest in defence, build offence, or stay out of it?

title: Power for the next decade
text: Demand keeps rising. Build abundant clean supply now, or let shortages decide.

title: Who owns the robots?
text: Robots now do real work. Someone collects the income.

options.label: Pay a robot dividend to citizens

title: When the jobs go
text: Unemployment is climbing and people are angry. What do you back?

title: An international AI treaty
text: Governments propose shared limits and inspections. Signing slows you down; refusing starts a race.
